statements.action_statement: Maintainer decision 2026-10-23: wait for Ubuntu to publish a grub2 build whose SBAT carries grub,6, then rebuild (make build), re-scan (make vulns) and re-test (make e2e). The grub generation is never raised by hand. Until then Secure Boot boots fail on PCs that applied SbatLevel 2025112400; documented in docs/SECURE_BOOT.md.

Maintainer decision 2026-10-23: wait for Ubuntu to publish a shim-signed build signed by the Microsoft UEFI CA 2023, then rebuild, re-scan and re-test. Until then Secure Boot boots fail on PCs whose db trusts only the 2023 CA; documented in docs/SECURE_BOOT.md.

Exploiting it needs someone at the GRUB console of the machine. Action: rebuild (make build) when Ubuntu publishes a fixed grub2 2.14 package, then re-scan.

statements.impact_statement: The flaw lets a device with a copied UUID bypass GRUB's password check. beast-booter's GRUB configuration sets no superusers and no password (grub/ has no 'set superusers' or password_pbkdf2), so there is no password check to bypass.
poplib is never imported: the bundled Python runs only the beast-booter app (installer/beastbooter, packaging/portable), which has no poplib import.
expat 2.8.5 is in the Windows runtime only. The app parses XML only in installer/beastbooter/platforms/darwin.py (plistlib, macOS), so on Windows pyexpat's XML_ParseBuffer is never called.

statements.action_statement: Portable app runtime, not on the drive; the installer uses tempfile.TemporaryDirectory for its own temporary folders. python-build-standalone 20261021 is the newest release: move packaging/portable/runtimes.lock to the first release that includes the fix (asset names, URLs and SHA-256 from its SHA256SUMS), rebuild the portable packages and re-scan.

statements.impact_statement: The flaw is in gz_vacate (gzwrite with non-blocking writes). None of the 62 ELF files in the beast-net initramfs imports gzwrite, gzopen, gzdopen, gzprintf, gzputs, gzputc, gzflush or gzclose_w (checked with readelf --dyn-syms on dist/esp/beast-net/initrd.img, 0.1.0); CPython's zlib module uses only the deflate/inflate API.
